reason: Trivia ('legs on a spider'); rewritten as a CSE-style heads-and-legs word problem.

fields.text: A backyard has chickens and goats. There are 20 heads and 56 legs in all. How many goats are there?
fields.explanation: If all 20 were chickens there would be 40 legs; the extra 16 legs come from goats at 2 extra legs each, so 16 ÷ 2 = 8 goats.
fields.steps:
1. Let c = chickens, g = goats: c + g = 20 and 2c + 4g = 56.
2. If all 20 were chickens: 20 × 2 = 40 legs.
3. Extra legs: 56 − 40 = 16.
4. Each goat adds 2 extra legs: 16 ÷ 2 = 8 goats.
5. Check: 12 chickens × 2 + 8 goats × 4 = 24 + 32 = 56 ✓
fields.hint: Pretend every animal is a chicken, then see how many legs are left over.
fields.whyA: 12 is the number of chickens, not goats.
fields.whyB: 6 goats would give 14 chickens and 28 + 24 = 52 legs, not 56.
fields.whyC: 10 goats would give 10 chickens and 20 + 40 = 60 legs, not 56.
fields.explanationTl: Kung lahat manok, 40 legs lang. Ang sobrang 16 legs ay galing sa kambing, tig-2 extra bawat isa, kaya 16 ÷ 2 = 8 goats.
fields.stepsTl:
1. c + g = 20 at 2c + 4g = 56.
2. Kung lahat manok: 20 × 2 = 40 legs.
3. Sobra: 56 − 40 = 16.
4. Bawat kambing may 2 extra legs: 16 ÷ 2 = 8 goats.
5. Check: 12 × 2 + 8 × 4 = 24 + 32 = 56 ✓
fields.hintTl: Isipin munang lahat ay manok, tapos tingnan kung ilang legs ang sobra.

reason: One of five near-duplicate 'n workers, n jobs, n days' items; rewritten as a working-together problem.

fields.text: Pedro can paint a room in 6 hours, and Jose can paint the same room in 3 hours. Working together, how many hours will they take?
fields.explanation: Pedro paints 1/6 of the room per hour and Jose 1/3; together 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2 per hour, so 2 hours.
fields.steps:
1. Pedro's rate: 1/6 room per hour.
2. Jose's rate: 1/3 room per hour.
3. Together: 1/6 + 2/6 = 3/6 = 1/2 room per hour.
4. Time = 1 ÷ 1/2 = 2 hours.
fields.hint: Add their rates (part of the job per hour), not their times.
fields.whyA: 4.5 is the average of 6 and 3; working together is faster than either one alone.
fields.whyB: 9 adds the two times; together they should finish faster, not slower.
fields.whyD: 3 is Jose's time alone; Pedro's help makes it shorter.
fields.explanationTl: Si Pedro 1/6 ng room kada oras, si Jose 1/3. Sabay: 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2 kada oras, kaya 2 hours.
fields.stepsTl:
1. Pedro: 1/6 kada oras.
2. Jose: 1/3 kada oras.
3. Sabay: 1/6 + 2/6 = 1/2 kada oras.
4. Time = 1 ÷ 1/2 = 2 hours.
fields.hintTl: I-add ang rates nila (bahagi ng trabaho kada oras), hindi ang oras.

fields.text: 6 workers can finish a road repair in 10 days. Working at the same rate, how many days will 15 workers take?
fields.steps:

2. With 15 workers: 60 ÷ 15 = 4 days.
fields.hint: More workers means fewer days: find the total worker-days first.
fields.whyA: 25 treats it as a direct proportion (10 × 15 ÷ 6); more workers should mean fewer days.
fields.whyC: 6 is the original number of workers, not the new number of days.
fields.whyD: 5 just halves the days; 15 workers is 2.5 times as many, so days are divided by 2.5.
fields.explanationTl: Ang trabaho ay 6 × 10 = 60 worker-days. Hatiin sa 15 workers: 60 ÷ 15 = 4 days.
fields.stepsTl:
1. Total work = 6 × 10 = 60 worker-days.
2. Sa 15 workers: 60 ÷ 15 = 4 days.
fields.hintTl: Mas maraming workers, mas kaunting araw. Hanapin muna ang total worker-days.

reason: Near-duplicate of id 33274110 (same doubling trick); rewritten as a fill-and-drain work problem.

fields.text: A pipe can fill a tank in 4 hours, while a drain can empty it in 12 hours. If both are open, how many hours will it take to fill the empty tank?
fields.explanation: Net rate = 1/4 − 1/12 = 3/12 − 1/12 = 2/12 = 1/6 tank per hour, so it takes 6 hours.
fields.steps:
1. Pipe fills 1/4 tank per hour.
2. Drain empties 1/12 tank per hour.
3. Net: 3/12 − 1/12 = 2/12 = 1/6 tank per hour.
4. Time = 1 ÷ 1/6 = 6 hours.
fields.hint: The drain works against the pipe, so subtract its rate.
fields.whyA: 3 adds the two rates (1/4 + 1/12 = 1/3); the drain takes water out, so subtract.
fields.whyB: 8 subtracts the times (12 − 4); subtract the rates instead.
fields.whyC: 16 adds the times (4 + 12); work problems combine rates, not times.
fields.explanationTl: Net rate = 1/4 − 1/12 = 1/6 ng tank kada oras, kaya 6 hours bago mapuno.
fields.stepsTl:
1. Pipe: 1/4 tank kada oras.
2. Drain: 1/12 tank kada oras (bawas).
3. Net: 3/12 − 1/12 = 1/6 kada oras.
4. Time = 1 ÷ 1/6 = 6 hours.
fields.hintTl: Kontra ang drain sa pipe, kaya i-subtract ang rate nito.
